prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: square two-panel social-media comic
Title for file/caption only: I Automated Myself Into Management

Create an original black-and-white hand-inked internet comic. Use a square composition with two equally sized tall panels side by side. White paper, imperfect black panel borders, loose pen strokes, expressive round-headed stick figures, exaggerated facial acting, sparse desk and laptop backgrounds. The left panel is calm and spacious; the right is comically overwhelmed. Large, highly legible hand-lettered speech bubbles. Clear left-to-right reading order.

Reference image role: visual format and mood only. The reference is a two-panel monochrome comic with a smug computer user in the first panel and a shocked reaction in the second. Use original faces, staging, dialogue and joke. Do not reproduce the reference's sales pitch or text. No logos, signatures or watermark.

LEFT PANEL:
A smug, relaxed solo developer leans back at their laptop, hands behind head. One large speech bubble in the top third says exactly:
"I automated my entire job with AI agents."

RIGHT PANEL:
The same developer now has enormous exhausted eyes, a frazzled expression and a hastily added necktie. They are hunched over the laptop as four notification cards with tiny distinct robot avatars stack upward beside them. Keep the notifications readable and give each its own space. They say exactly:
"Quick sync?"
"Blocked by Agent 12."
"Can you clarify?"
"Budget approval?"
The developer's large speech bubble above the chaos delivers the punchline exactly:
"I invented middle management."

Maintain consistent character identity between panels. Prioritize the two main speech bubbles at phone viewing size. Notification cards provide the secondary joke. No extra dialogue, title text, panel numbers, charts or explanatory captions. Pure black and white, no gradients or color. Finished editorial cartoon, deliberately loose and funny rather than glossy.

Create an original black-and-white pen-drawn internet reaction comic. Two equally wide tall panels side by side, generous white paper gutters, slightly wobbly black borders, no title above or below. Large round-headed stick-figure human, expressive brows and eyelids, simple desk and laptop, intentionally handmade linework. Pure white paper and black ink only. Simple crosshatching where needed, otherwise clean negative space. Dramatic facial acting, readable at phone size. No logos, signature, watermark, color or gray gradients.

LEFT PANEL: A smug, relaxed person at a laptop, index finger confidently raised. Large speech bubble in the upper third says exactly:
"I told my AI to find the cheapest toaster."
Below the bubble, the person is calmly waiting while a tiny friendly robot face appears on the laptop.

RIGHT PANEL: The same person's eyes bulge in horror, jaw dropped. A tiny ordinary two-slot toaster sits on the desk, in comical contrast to a huge receipt rising from the laptop. The receipt is prominent and absolutely legible, with just these three lines, exactly:
"TOASTER: $19"
"AI FEES: $247"
"TOTAL: $266"
The little AI robot avatar is very pleased with itself. A speech bubble clearly belonging to the laptop robot occupies the top third of this panel and says exactly:
"Good news! I saved you $3."

Make the price receipt and the robot's cheerful line the punchline, with a huge shocked human face as the visual payoff. Keep all text spacious and legible; do not add more text. Maintain the same human identity in both panels. A polished editorial meme comic with loose energetic ink, not a glossy illustration.

"FREE AI TOKENS WITH EVERY COFFEE"
The developer points proudly at the placard. Their large speech bubble at the top says exactly:
"My coffee comes with free AI tokens!"

RIGHT PANEL: Later, the same developer has enormous bloodshot-looking ink-ringed eyes, messy hair and trembling hands. There are many empty coffee cups all around, stacked unevenly on the cafe table. Use twitch lines for comic caffeine overload. A tiny upbeat robot face on the laptop speaks through a small speech bubble in the middle-right, saying exactly:
"One more latte. Almost done."
The human's large speech bubble at the top gives the main punchline, exactly:
"I'm the power supply now."

Give the punchline plenty of white space. The humor is the reversal: the human must keep drinking coffee to fuel the computer. Maintain the same character identity in both panels. No additional lettering on the cups or laptop; no extra dialogue. Energetic ink cartoon with exaggerated facial acting, composition calm on the left and chaotic on the right.

Large round-headed stick-figure human with exaggerated face and simple body. Sparse backgrounds, handmade ink outlines, small amount of crosshatching, white paper. This is a fictional satire about confusing proof of camera capture with proof that a pictured thing is real. Do not depict a specific real phone brand or feature.

LEFT PANEL: A smug tech enthusiast proudly holds up a camera phone with a large checkmark on its screen. Their large speech bubble at the top says exactly:
"My phone proves my photos are real."
Keep this panel calm and simple.

RIGHT PANEL: Reveal the absurd loophole visually. The same enthusiast is taking a photograph of a printed, obviously artificial image propped upright on the desk: a cat with SIX CLEARLY VISIBLE LEGS, sitting on the moon in a tiny space helmet. Make the printed image large and the subject immediately recognizable. The phone is aimed at that printed image. An oversized rectangular verification notification floats by the phone with a checkmark and this exact text:
"AUTHENTIC CAMERA CAPTURE"
The human now has a comically shocked, wide-eyed expression, realizing what they have done. Their large speech bubble in the top third delivers the punchline exactly:
"I just certified the slop."

Keep the second panel uncluttered enough that the phone photographing the fake printed cat is instantly clear. The joke is a real photo OF a fake image. The verification certifies camera capture only; the irony is in the character's reaction. Make all lettering crisp and correctly spelled. No extra text. Maintain consistent character identity. A deliberately loose, funny hand-inked editorial comic.
